text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended higher but failed to make further headway on the upside in the afternoon despite advancing New York-listed arabica futures. Traders said spot May was kept through the day at $1,650 a tonne on origin hedge selling, notably from Indonesia. May last hit the $1,650 mark on April 1. Indonesia, faced with growing supplies from its new crop harvest, had been absent in the last few days awaiting more lucrative prices. Nevertheless, the market still finished up on balance on earlier speculative and trade buying. May and benchmark July were each up $20 at $1,640 and $1,663 respectively.

Arabica futures in New York ended higher for the third session in a row with the nearby May contract seeing a fresh life of contract high intra-day, though volumes were only moderate. The spot May contract ended up 6.75 cents at 216.55 cents/lb, after seeing a new contract high earlier at 218 cents/lb. But the first notice day for May is April 22 and the July contract now has more open interest. July coffee ended up 6.65 cents at 194.15 cents/lb, after seeing a session high at 194.50 cents. The May/July spread ended little changed though at 22.50 cents, not far from Wednesday's contract highs of 22.75 cents.
After Friday's close, the CSCE reported warehouse stocks of 63,249 60-kg bags as of April 17, down from 67,578 bags on April 16. There were 500 bags pending grading in New York, the CSCE added.

BRAZIL - Port workers agreed to end a 48-hour nationwide strike and said they would return to work immediately after a partial agreement at a Santos steel mill was reached with management, union officials said. The national strike, which began at 0700 on April 18, had little effect on agricultural commodities as many ports operated normally.

UNITED STATES - For the week ended April 12, green coffee roastings totalled approximately 335,000 60-kg bags, up from 290,000 bags the previous week and compared with 330,000 bags in the corresponding week a year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage reports. Cumulative roastings so far totalled 5.100 mn bags, compared to 4.490 mn bags in the same period a year ago.

COLOMBIA - Colombia's main truck drivers' union began a nationwide strike at midnight on Saturday after two last-ditch attempts by the government to avert the work stoppage failed to produce agreement over key demands, union officials said. The ACC represents about 80 per cent of Colombia's truck drivers. It called the strike in March on grounds that both the government and private companies had violated terms of a pact that ended a crippling 11-day ACC strike last October. That strike, which brought most highway freight to a standstill and wreaked havoc with exports of coffee ended with a pledge to increase freight rates by 18 per cent in January.

PORTUGAL - Coffee imports in November 1996 amounted to 56,991 60-kg bags, down from 59,503 bags imported in November 1995. This brought cumulative imports in January/November 1996 up to 678,342 bags, almost 18 per cent up on the volume imported in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 reached 629,621 bags against 663,813 bags in 1994. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/November 1996 were Ivory Coast (99,000 vs 74,600 bags) and Brazil (90,500 vs 80,200 bags).
